issue_4_detail.complaint: A301 (or any Alpha) can appear as active despite lacking ticker-specific evidence AND local structure support.
issue_4_detail.bug_classification: A (scorer/classifier-stage decision-logic bug) -- specifically in comqutor_alpha/graph_engine/alpha_level_classifier.py's Case A/B qualification logic. NOT a persistence bug, NOT an API serialization bug, NOT a display normalization bug, NOT a frontend rendering bug -- all four traced and confirmed correct-by-construction (see trace below).

trace.activation_scorer_v2.py: UNCHANGED. Already correctly computed the score and cap_reason_codes (NO_TICKER_SPECIFIC_EVIDENCE, NO_LOCAL_STRUCTURE_SUPPORT) -- the caps only reduced the score ceiling to 60/70, both still above ACTIVE_THRESHOLD=50, which is exactly why an under-qualified Alpha could still clear 'active'.
trace.alpha_level_classifier.py (THE BUG, NOW: Case A/B previously never gated 'active' at all (a prior, now-superseded Product decision). Fixed: when BOTH required signals are absent, qualified_level demotes ACTIVE -> CANDIDATE (the only lower canonical level), is_blocked=True, blocked_from=('active',). A single missing signal alone does NOT gate (matches John's literal 'lacks both' wording). B4 thresholds (50/70/86) untouched.
trace.persistence (week4_persistence.py): Verified: generic _text()/_bool() pass-through of qualified_level/is_blocked/blocked_from -- no remapping logic exists that could rewrite the fixed classifier's output.
trace.API serialization (routes_research.py): Verified: activation_summary/entity_exposure sections reuse v2_alphas verbatim, never recompute a second qualification algorithm.
trace.display normalization (alpha_display_nor: Verified via _activation_level_for(): returns CAPPED_ACTIVE only when qualified_level==ACTIVE and blocked from DOMINANT; otherwise returns qualified_level verbatim. For the fixed case (qualified_level=CANDIDATE), it correctly falls through to 'candidate' -- proven by a new end-to-end test running the REAL classifier into the REAL normalizer.
trace.frontend (AlphaCard.tsx): Verified: `const displayLevel = activation?.activation_level ?? status` reads the authoritative field directly, no independent score-threshold logic; already has a built-in 'Held at {qualified_level}, blocked from {blocked_from}' rendering path for exactly this scenario (target_level !== qualified_level).

conflict_state_separation_detail.requirement: Strict ADMITTED / CANDIDATE / BLOCKED-REJECTED separation; no candidate as admitted; no blocked/rejected as Main Conflict; Main Conflict only from admitted; API/UI/artifact counts agree.
conflict_state_separation_detail.already_correct_from_prior_work: conflict_detector.py's admitted_conflicts list (and therefore conflicts/main_conflict) is built ONLY from pairs whose outcome=='admitted' -- structurally impossible for a suppressed/rejected/candidate pair to leak in. The B2 Conflict Evidence Admissibility gate (conflict_admissibility.py) already produces a strict two-value status (admitted/candidate) layered under the three-value outcome (admitted/suppressed/rejected); a B2-denied 'candidate' pair's outcome is always 'suppressed', never 'admitted'. The run-audit API layer (_conflict_summary_section) already exposed explicit per-pair 'outcome'/'admissibility.status'/'is_main' fields and top-level declared/admitted/suppressed/rejected/candidate counts from prior work (B2_CONFLICT_EVIDENCE_ADMISSIBILITY).
conflict_state_separation_detail.new_this_task: Two new accounting invariants (_conflict_accounting_invariants): conflict_pairs_conserved (declared == admitted+suppressed+rejected) and candidate_conflicts_are_a_subset_of_suppressed. 3 new tests in tests/test_run_audit_v2.py proving PASS on a consistent fixture, FAIL surfaces honestly on a tampered one, and a B2-denied candidate pair is counted correctly and never becomes main_conflict.
conflict_state_separation_detail.verified_on_real_data: Both regenerated real NVDA run_audit.json files show conflict_pairs_conserved=PASS.
